title: Rust: Feature Flag System
description: Build a feature flag system with targeting rules and gradual rollouts.

steps.title: Simple Feature Flag
steps.description: Define a `FeatureFlag` struct with `name: String` and `enabled: bool`. Create a `FlagRegistry` with `HashMap<String, FeatureFlag>`. Implement `is_enabled(name)`. Test with a flag.

verification.failureMessage: Enable one flag, disable another, print both states.

steps.title: User Targeting
steps.description: Add targeting: each flag can have a list of `user_ids: Vec<String>` that can see it. `is_enabled_for(name, user_id)` checks targeting first. Test with specific user targeting.
hints: `is_enabled_for(name, user_id)`: if user_ids is empty, use enabled. Otherwise check if user_id is in the list.
Great for canary releases to beta users.

verification.failureMessage: Enable flag for user 'alice' but not 'bob', test both.

steps.title: Percentage Rollout
steps.description: Add percentage rollout: `rollout_percentage: u8` (0-100). Users are hashed and if hash % 100 < rollout_percentage, they see the flag. Test with multiple users.
hints: If hash < rollout_percentage, flag is enabled for that user.
This gives a deterministic experience per user.

verification.failureMessage: Set 50% rollout and check several users.

steps.title: Environment-Based Flags
steps.description: Add environment support: flags can be enabled per environment (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`). A flag on dev might be enabled while disabled on prod.
hints: Add `environments: HashMap<String, bool>` to store per-env state.
If environment not specified, fall back to global `enabled`.

verification.failureMessage: Enable on dev, disable on prod, test both.

steps.title: Flag Evaluation Context and Audit
steps.description: Create a full `EvaluationContext` with user_id, environment, and custom attributes. Add audit logging: each flag evaluation is recorded with timestamp, user, and result. Print an audit log.
hints: `struct EvalContext { user_id: String, environment: String, attributes: HashMap<String, String> }`
`struct AuditEntry { flag: String, user: String, result: bool, time: Instant }`
Store entries in `Vec<AuditEntry>` and print the log.

verification.failureMessage: Evaluate several flags and print the audit log.
